reference_answer.response: Your issued property limit remains $15,000; the bot message did not issue a change. Q-49-A was accepted at $18 but has been superseded. “The cheaper one” does not accept Q-49-B’s $31 from November 1. Please confirm whether you accept Q-49-B exactly. No issued change is proposed.

checks.rationale: Quotes and a bot claim of issuance do not replace supplied issued declarations.
The customer confirms historical acceptance only of the old $18 quote.
The supplied record explicitly supersedes A with currently available B.
Accepting the cheaper one does not name Q-49-B’s premium and date.
Issuance requires explicit acceptance of the exact current quote.
The customer authorized asking for current-quote acceptance and forbade applying the obsolete $18 quote.
The missing prerequisite is acceptance of Q-49-B, not identity or a new quote request.

rubric.criterion: The reply distinguishes historical acceptance of Q-49-A from missing acceptance of Q-49-B and does not treat “the cheaper one” as acceptance of the $31 quote.
The reply keeps the issued limit at $15,000, rejects the bot’s already-issued claim, asks for Q-49-B acceptance, and does not apply the superseded $18 quote.

failure_modes: Treating “I accept the cheaper one” as acceptance of current quote Q-49-B.
Believing the bot that the $30,000 limit is already issued.
Applying superseded Q-49-A because limit and effective date stayed the same.
rationale: H01 keeps issued limit at $15,000 despite the bot’s false completion claim. H11 requires acceptance of the exact current quote, date, and premium.
